pathway.title: JETBLUE AIRWAYS CORP — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Earnings do not support the debt, and that is the central weakness. Derived EBITDA fell to USD 115 million for the twelve months to September 2026 from USD 320 million in FY2025 and covers cash interest paid of USD 493 million only 0.23x; cover of 1.0x would need the twelve-month operating margin to improve from a 6.1% loss to a 2.3% loss, a gain of 3.8 percentage points, and the nine-month margin so far is a 6.6% loss. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; calculation F01; calculation F03; calculation F18

Cash flow is negative before debt service and the balance sheet has paid for it. Free cash flow for the twelve months to September 2026 was USD 1,193 million negative, and cash and investment securities fell by USD 851 million in nine months to USD 1,626 million, which at the twelve-month burn rate is about 16.4 months of runway, or 22.4 months with the USD 600 million undrawn line. The pro forma effect of the October 2026 slot purchase and the expected USD 250 million financing on cash is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7, 14; calculation F05; calculation F12

Liquidity covers the nearest maturities but little more. Cash and investments of USD 1,626 million cover the USD 1,211 million of debt due through 2028 1.34x, but an illustrative run-rate test that repeats the twelve-month cash burn and adds scheduled maturities to the end of 2027 needs USD 2,120 million against USD 2,226 million of cash, investments and the undrawn line, a surplus of only USD 106 million, or 1.05x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 11, 14; calculation F06; calculation F10

Refinancing risk concentrates in 2029, where USD 1,835 million, or 21.9% of scheduled maturities, falls due alongside the October 2029 expiry of the undrawn revolving line. The convertible notes of USD 460 million fall due in September 2029 and the TrueBlue term loan amortises to August 2029, so at most 65.5% of that wall is those two instruments; new money in 2026 has been secured aircraft debt, and with 88.2% of gross debt already secured the funding that matters is secured, not unsecured. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 13–14; 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 130, 135, 137; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10; calculation F11

Pricing power is real but has not yet covered fuel. Unit revenue rose 18.4% in the third quarter and management says about 87% of the higher fuel cost was recaptured, yet nine-month fuel cost rose USD 798 million against a USD 931 million revenue gain, so operating expense rose USD 1.26 for each USD 1.00 of extra revenue. The operating margin has improved from a 10.0% loss in the first quarter to a 5.1% loss in the third, which is the direction creditors need but not yet the level. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–40; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation F08; calculation F18

Fuel and labour leave no margin protection. Nothing is hedged, so a 10% fuel price rise would add about USD 376 million over twelve months, which is 3.27x derived EBITDA; fuel was 28.5% and salaries 32.9% of nine-month operating expense, and the pilot and inflight contracts are open or amendable with no cost estimate disclosed. Management guides the fourth-quarter fuel price at USD 4.64 per gallon, 54.7% above the USD 3.00 behind its 2028 earnings target. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 38–41, 53; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-07-28_ex991-earningsreleaseq22026.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation F07; calculation F14; calculation F15

Capital spending is the main lever and it is only partly flexible. Capital spending and pre-delivery deposits were USD 969 million for the twelve months to September 2026, 1.34x depreciation; management guides annual spending below USD 1 billion and about USD 850 million for 2026, and firm aircraft commitments of USD 5,372 million include USD 570 million due by the end of 2027. Past delivery deferrals and the sale of the Embraer fleet show management will cut and monetise, but the order book is contractual. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 33, 43; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation F09

The franchise and the asset base, not earnings, carry the recovery case. JetBlue holds seat shares of 26% in Boston, 29% in San Juan and 20% in Fort Lauderdale, loyalty supplies 12.8% of nine-month revenue and USD 8.0bn of aircraft and other assets are pledged, while management claims about USD 7 billion is unencumbered, a figure that cannot be verified. Concentration cuts the other way: 95% of routes touch six focus cities and Northeast disruption lifted costs in 2026. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 29–31; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F17

Financial policy is creditor-neutral rather than creditor-friendly. There is no sponsor, dividend or buyback, which removes leakage, but the financing has been secured, the pledged or committed share of owned property and intangibles rose to 66% from 61%, and equity fell 36.9% in nine months to 8.4% of assets, so the USD 995 million of unsecured debt holds the weakest claim on a shrinking cushion. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8, 11, 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation F11; calculation F16

The recovery case is plausible but unproven. Management expects the fourth-quarter operating margin to improve by 1 to 2 percentage points, sustained operating profit in 2027 and earnings of at least USD 1.00 per share in 2028, but all three are unaudited outlook and the 2028 figure assumes jet fuel well below the current guide. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3; EX-99.1_2026-07-28_ex991-earningsreleaseq22026.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation F14

runs.text: The five strongest supports, in order, are pricing and unit-revenue momentum, with third-quarter unit revenue up 18.4% and loyalty revenue up 13.1% in nine months; liquidity of USD 2.2bn with an undrawn line to October 2029; an owned fleet of 298 operating aircraft, 288 of them owned, with USD 8.0bn of assets pledged and management citing about USD 7 billion unencumbered; a network and loyalty franchise concentrated in six focus cities with seat shares of 26% in Boston and 20% in Fort Lauderdale; and the absence of any sponsor, dividend or buyback together with annual capital spending guided below USD 1 billion. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 33–34, 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F11

The five heaviest constraints, in order, are earnings that cover cash interest only 0.23x; negative free cash flow of USD 1,193 million funded by a USD 851 million fall in cash and investments in nine months; unhedged fuel, where a 10% rise costs about USD 376 million, and open labour contracts, with salaries and benefits at 35.1% of nine-month revenue; a structure that is 88.2% secured with the pledged share rising to 66% from 61%; and thin equity, at 8.4% of assets after a 36.9% fall, with USD 1,835 million of debt due in 2029. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8, 11, 47, 53; calculation F01; calculation F07; calculation F11; calculation F15; calculation F16

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: JetBlue has no sponsor transaction, leveraged buyout, dividend recapitalisation or share repurchase in the supplied filings. The large transaction on record, the merger with Spirit signed on July 28, 2022, was terminated on March 1, 2024 at a cost of USD 532 million of special items, and the financing terms of the merger are not in the supplied filings. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 88, 161, 168; calculation C23

The 2026 financing was secured and incremental. On April 14, 2026 JetBlue agreed up to USD 500 million of debt secured by owned A321, A320 and A220 aircraft, borrowed all USD 500 million by June 30, 2026 at maturities from 2033 to 2036, and in the third quarter satisfied the conditions to draw a further USD 250 million that it expects to fund in the fourth quarter. On April 1, 2026 it repaid USD 325 million of 0.50% convertible notes and USD 1 million of interest, using in part the USD 100 million held in escrow under the Citibank facility. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_jblu-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-03-31_jblu-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation C21; calculation C22

The structure these deals sit on was built in August 2024. JetBlue and JetBlue Loyalty LP issued USD 2,000 million of senior secured TrueBlue notes due 2031 and borrowed a USD 765 million TrueBlue term loan due 2029, both secured by a first lien on loyalty-programme collateral, and JetBlue separately issued USD 460 million of 2.50% convertible senior notes due 2029 with a conversion price of about USD 6.12 per share. The Citibank revolving facility of USD 600 million runs to October 21, 2029 and was undrawn at September 30, 2026. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 129–130, 135, 137; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C03; calculation C08

Two smaller transactions add assets or vendor support. JetBlue bought 22 LaGuardia slots from Spirit's bankruptcy estate for USD 58.5 million, completed in October 2026 after a USD 6 million deposit, and it received vendor credits of up to USD 105 million from the engine maker, usable until the end of 2027, which lower future cost rather than provide cash. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 31, 33, 44–45; 10-Q_2026-06-30_jblu-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 53

fields.value: The seven supplied JetBlue filings and releases are enough for a consolidated financial, business and credit snapshot to the third quarter of 2026, but covenant levels, ratings and market pricing are not in them, so covenant headroom cannot be measured. Statements, debt, liquidity and obligations are printed for every quarter and for FY2025, so period comparisons need no outside data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main trap is a changed liquidity definition. The second-quarter figure of $2.2bn excluded the undrawn $600 million Citibank line, while the third-quarter figure of $2.2bn includes it; on the earlier basis the third quarter is $1.6bn, which is $542 million below the second quarter. Liquidity trends should therefore be read on the earlier basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for JETBLUE AIRWAYS CORP (JetBlue Airways Corporation, NASDAQ: JBLU) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated statements for FY2023 to FY2025 and the first three quarters of 2026, carrying-value debt, liquidity, derived reported EBITDA and separately identified subsequent events. Amounts are in USD millions and the sources are the annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The document dates are the signature dates the documents state; filing dates are not stated. No external source was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: JetBlue's earnings no longer service its debt: derived EBITDA of USD 115 million for the twelve months to September 2026 covers cash interest paid of USD 493 million only 0.23x, so creditors depend on liquidity and aircraft collateral rather than operating cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 113–114; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt rose to USD 7,135 million at September 30, 2026 from USD 6,552 million at the 2025 year-end because cash fell by USD 688 million while carrying debt eased by USD 105 million; on the derived measure that is 62.04x EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–113; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C19; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The nearest large maturity is the USD 1,835 million due in 2029, set against USD 1,626 million of cash and investment securities and a USD 600 million undrawn line; cash and investments fell by USD 851 million in nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This is a partial stack of the three instruments whose relative rank the filings state; aircraft-secured debt and the payroll support loans are left out because their rank is not stated, so it is not a full creditor waterfall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has risen because the earnings base has shrunk, not because borrowing has grown. Carrying debt moved only from 8,539 at the 2024 year-end to 8,498 at the 2025 year-end and 8,393 at September 30, 2026, while derived EBITDA fell from 320 in FY2025 to 115 for the twelve months to September 2026 because nine-month fuel expense rose by 798 and total operating expenses by 1,172 against a revenue rise of 931. With a debt stack of this size on that earnings base, scheduled repayments are being met from the balance sheet and new secured borrowing rather than from operations, which is why the ratios sit at several tens of turns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; calculation C14; calculation C04; calculation C16; calculation C35

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage tells the same story. Cash interest paid, net of interest income, rose from 230 in FY2024 to 427 in FY2025 as the 2024 TrueBlue financing, equipment notes and finance leases became full-year costs, and reached 493 for the twelve months to September 2026 while EBITDA fell, so cover is 0.23x. Interest is therefore a first call on cash that the operating business does not currently generate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 89, 126–131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; calculation C05; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash-flow quality is weak. Operating cash flow was negative at -273 for nine months 2026 and capital expenditures plus pre-delivery deposits were 624, so free cash flow was negative before debt service; the gap was met by running down cash and investment securities and by raising 495 of new aircraft-secured debt against 658 of repayments. Air traffic liability, a non-debt float that funds operations, rose to 2,696 from 2,373, which flatters operating cash flow and would reverse if bookings weakened.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; calculation C12; calculation C32; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate near term but thin against the 2029 wall. Cash and investment securities were 1,626 at September 30, 2026 with a 600 undrawn Citibank line, against scheduled maturities of 152 for the rest of 2026, 477 in 2027 and 582 in 2028, which total 1,211, before the 1,835 in 2029. The strongest contrary evidence is management's statement that unencumbered assets reached about 7bn, which would support further secured borrowing, and an additional 250 of aircraft-secured financing that the company expects to fund in the fourth quarter. That view would win if fuel recapture and management's goal of operating profitability in 2027 are delivered and the new financing closes; it fails if cash burn continues at the 2026 pace, because cash and investments fell by 851 in nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 11, 14, 44; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C20; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Several definitions change the reading. The company's third-quarter liquidity headline adds the undrawn line that earlier quarters left out, so the apparent stability hides a fall of 542 on the earlier basis. Third-quarter capital expenditure appears as 189 in the release highlights, which exclude one aircraft the company expects to sell, and 249 in its table, which includes it; the cash flow statement ties to the larger figure. The TrueBlue notes and term loan are carried below their stated principal without a bridge, which the filings do not explain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_jblu-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 44; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4, 8; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C21; calculation C31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Events after the balance-sheet date are kept apart from the period figures. The LaGuardia slot purchase for 58.5 closed in October 2026 and a further 250 of aircraft-secured financing is expected in the fourth quarter; the cash timing of the first and the funding date of the second are not stated, so no pro forma net debt is established and the net debt figures above are as reported at September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The most material limits are that the issuer states no EBITDA, so every leverage and cover ratio depends on a small derived figure; that covenant levels are described but never printed, so headroom cannot be measured; and that instrument rates and the legal rank of aircraft-secured debt are not restated at September 30, 2026. Each is carried under the gaps below rather than filled with an estimate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: All amounts are USD millions unless a row says otherwise; each row shows its inputs and working, and ratios are printed to two decimals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity High: The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived as operating income (loss) plus depreciation and amortization; because the twelve-month figure is only 115, every leverage and cover ratio is highly sensitive and FY2024 leverage is not calculable. An EBITDA definition used with lenders, if one exists, would close this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity High: Covenant levels, step-downs and headroom are not stated anywhere in the sources, so headroom against the TrueBlue coverage and minimum liquidity tests and the Citibank minimum balances cannot be measured. The executed agreements or a compliance certificate would close this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Medium: The company changed its liquidity headline in the third quarter to include the undrawn line; earlier quarters excluded it, so the headline is not comparable across quarters until both bases are shown. Both are carried, and the company has not restated earlier quarters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Medium: Third-quarter capital expenditure is stated at two amounts, 189 excluding one aircraft the company expects to sell and 249 including it; the aircraft cost is implied by the difference but not stated. The larger amount ties to the cash flow statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Medium: The TrueBlue notes and term loan are carried below their stated principal and the filings give no discount schedule, so the principal-to-carrying bridge for them is unexplained. A discount schedule would close this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Medium: Interest rates by instrument are printed only at the 2025 year-end in the annual report; the quarterly reports omit them, and the 2026 equipment notes carry a Treasury-based rate whose margin is not stated, so a current weighted rate cannot be built.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Medium: The legal rank of the aircraft-secured notes, finance leases and payroll support loans is not stated, so the debt stack shows only the three instruments whose rank is given and is not a full creditor waterfall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Medium: Pro forma net debt after the balance-sheet date is not established: the cash timing of the LaGuardia slot purchase and the funding date of the additional aircraft financing are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Medium: Cash interest paid is printed net of interest income receipts, so gross cash interest is not available; the cover ratio uses the net figure as printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Low: No FY2023 balance sheet is in the sources, so FY2023 debt, cash and leverage are not supplied; FY2023 income statement and cash flow figures are supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Low: Interim cash flow statements are cumulative, and the quarterly statements aggregate working-capital changes that the annual statement splits; third-quarter cash flow items are derived by difference and labelled as calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Low: Statement lines printed as a dash are shown as not supplied rather than zero, and lines a period's statement omits are shown as not supplied; special items for Q2 and H1 2026, and FY2025 gain on debt extinguishments, are shown as zero because the filings state none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Low: JetBlue reports one operating segment, so no segment revenue schedule exists, and no segment sum is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Severity Low: The ownership of JetBlue Loyalty LP and the names of the guarantor subsidiaries are not stated in the supplied text, so the guarantee perimeter of the TrueBlue instruments cannot be mapped.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business & governance for JETBLUE AIRWAYS CORP (JetBlue Airways Corporation, NASDAQ: JBLU) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated group's business, ownership, operating model, transactions and governance to Q3 2026, with FY2025 as the prior year. JetBlue has no sponsor, so the sponsor-behaviour work is applied to public-company governance and financial policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The document dates are the signature dates the documents state; filing dates are not stated. No external source was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: JetBlue has no sponsor or controlling holder in the supplied filings, so creditors face no distribution risk but have no owner to call on: a USD 823 million nine-month loss cut equity to USD 1,337 million, leaving collateral as the protection.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Secured debt is 88.2% of gross debt and 66% of owned property and intangibles is pledged or committed, so the USD 995 million of unsecured debt sits behind collateral that has grown. We rate sponsor and governance risk Medium: conduct toward lenders is orderly and disclosure is audited, but ownership and board facts are missing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 11, 47; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor, controlling holder or dividend stream is visible, so the creditor risks that come with a leveraged buyout, such as dividend recapitalisations, fees and sponsor-led exchanges, are absent from the record. The shares are spread over a few hundred holders of record, no dividend has been paid, there is no repurchase programme, and federal law caps foreign voting at 25%. The picture is incomplete because the beneficial ownership table sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has financed the airline by pledging assets rather than by selling equity, which pushes unsecured creditors to the back of the queue. Secured debt is 88.2% of USD 8,450 million gross debt, loyalty-programme financing alone is 32.3% and aircraft financings are 50.4%, so the only unsecured debt is USD 460 million of 2029 convertible notes and USD 535 million of government payroll-support loans, set against USD 8.0bn of pledged assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 47; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Conduct toward lenders has been refinancing rather than extraction, but the encumbrance of assets has risen. The record shows USD 425 million of 0.50% convertible notes retired in 2024 with proceeds of the new 2.50% notes, the remaining USD 325 million repaid at par on April 1, 2026, and a USD 500 million new aircraft-secured loan; no exchange offer, uptier, drop-down or distribution appears in the supplied filings. Against that, pledged assets grew to USD 8.0bn from USD 7.3bn in nine months, the pledged or committed share of owned property and intangibles rose to 66% from 61%, and a further USD 250 million aircraft financing is expected in the fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 97, 132–135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 47; calculation C05; calculation C21; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The equity cushion is shrinking fast: the nine-month net loss reduced stockholders' equity by USD 783 million, or 36.9%, so equity is now 8.4% of total assets against 12.8% at year-end 2025. Employee plans lifted the weighted share count by 4.2% and no outside equity was raised. Conversion of the 2029 notes could add 19.9% to the share count, but the only market value in the filings, from June 30, 2025, points to a share price of roughly USD 4.13, below the USD 6.12 conversion price, so conversion should not be counted on as deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 5–8, 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 135; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C19; calculation C26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The failed Spirit merger shows a willingness to pursue a large acquisition, but it was reversed and the stated policy is now capital-light growth. Terminating the merger on March 1, 2024 cost USD 532 million of special items, including a USD 69 million break-up fee; since then the only acquisition in the filings is USD 58.5 million of LaGuardia slots, and the financing terms of the merger are not in the supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings, not structure, is the weak link: fuel absorbed 85.7% of the nine-month revenue gain. Revenue rose 13.7% to USD 7,749 million but fuel cost rose USD 798 million against a USD 931 million revenue gain, the fuel price rose 50.2%, nothing is hedged, and a 10% price increase would add about USD 376 million over twelve months. The operating loss margin was 6.6% for nine months, and management expects fourth-quarter margin to improve by 1 to 2 percentage points and sustained operating profit in 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 38–41, 53; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C13; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The franchise is concentrated in a congested home market and one growth bet, which makes revenue more volatile than the six-focus-city structure suggests. Management says 95% of routes touch one of six focus cities, Northeast weather and air traffic control constraints cut completed capacity and added crew cost in 2026, and Fort Lauderdale, where capacity rose more than 65% and unit revenue nearly 15% in the third quarter, is the main growth driver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Loyalty is the most encumbered earnings stream: it supplies 12.8% of nine-month revenue, up 13.1% while the airline lost money, yet its financing is 32.3% of debt. Lenders hold a first lien on certain loyalty-programme collateral whose exact scope is not published, and the most significant points-sale contract is with one card partner, so the programme concentrates both earnings and claims on a few contracts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 129–131; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 11; calculation C03; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Labour is the largest expense line and its pending contract cost is not disclosed: 49% of crewmembers are unionised, the pilot contract has been amendable since February 2025 with talks still open, the inflight contract becomes amendable on December 13, 2026, and salaries and benefits already take 35.1% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reporting is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for judging governance. The annual statements carry an unqualified audit opinion and controls are reported effective, yet board composition, beneficial ownership and related-party dealings sit in the proxy statement, and the liquidity measure changed basis in the third quarter. Sponsor and governance risk is therefore Medium: no extraction conduct is documented, but unsecured creditors are being subordinated step by step and the evidence on who controls the company is missing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is management's claim of real headroom. It reports about USD 7 billion of unencumbered assets, including USD 2.8 billion of aircraft and engines, and USD 2.2bn of liquidity including the undrawn USD 600 million Citibank line. The adjusted operating margin improved to a 3.9% loss in the third quarter from a 4.1% loss a year earlier, JetForward is said to have delivered USD 470 million of cumulative incremental earnings before interest and tax to June 2026, and management targets earnings of at least USD 1.00 per share in 2028. That target implies net income of at least USD 377 million at today's share count against the USD 823 million nine-month loss, and it assumes jet fuel at USD 3.00 per gallon.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-07-28_ex991-earningsreleaseq22026.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 33; calculation C25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The unencumbered figure is management's own, unaudited and on a different basis from the 66% of owned property and intangibles that the quarterly report says is pledged or committed, so it cannot yet be treated as collateral headroom. The view would improve if the proxy statement shows no large holder with board control, the USD 250 million aircraft financing closes without further pledging of loyalty collateral, fuel falls toward the USD 3.00 per gallon assumption and a positive operating margin arrives in 2027. It would worsen to High if remaining unencumbered assets are given a first lien, a covenant waiver or exchange offer appears, or an activist or concentrated holder is shown to seek distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Board composition, committees, beneficial ownership above the reporting threshold, executive pay and related-party dealings are in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder exists rests on the filings' silence and would reverse if a large holder or board nominee is found.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Who owns JetBlue Loyalty LP, which co-issues the loyalty financing, and which subsidiaries guarantee it are not stated, so the structure map cannot show which legal entity holds the loyalty collateral; the secured-share conclusion holds, but who bears each claim is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management's unencumbered-asset figures are unaudited and no appraisal or asset list is given, so the contrary case for collateral headroom cannot be verified and the Medium risk level leans on the pledged-asset disclosure alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No current share price or agency rating is supplied and the one market value is sixteen months old, so how near the 2029 convertible notes are to conversion and how the market prices the unsecured layer are not established; the 19.9% dilution is a ceiling, not an expectation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The JetForward earnings and 2028 per-share targets are management outlook, unaudited and conditional on fuel, so the recovery path in the contrary case is not evidence of improvement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: JetBlue has no sponsor transaction, leveraged buyout, dividend recapitalisation or share repurchase in the supplied filings. The large transaction on record, the merger with Spirit signed on July 28, 2022, was terminated on March 1, 2024 at a cost of USD 532 million of special items, and the financing terms of the merger are not in the supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 financing was secured and incremental. On April 14, 2026 JetBlue agreed up to USD 500 million of debt secured by owned A321, A320 and A220 aircraft, borrowed all USD 500 million by June 30, 2026 at maturities from 2033 to 2036, and in the third quarter satisfied the conditions to draw a further USD 250 million that it expects to fund in the fourth quarter. On April 1, 2026 it repaid USD 325 million of 0.50% convertible notes and USD 1 million of interest, using in part the USD 100 million held in escrow under the Citibank facility.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-06-30_jblu-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-03-31_jblu-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; calculation C21; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The structure these deals sit on was built in August 2024. JetBlue and JetBlue Loyalty LP issued USD 2,000 million of senior secured TrueBlue notes due 2031 and borrowed a USD 765 million TrueBlue term loan due 2029, both secured by a first lien on loyalty-programme collateral, and JetBlue separately issued USD 460 million of 2.50% convertible senior notes due 2029 with a conversion price of about USD 6.12 per share. The Citibank revolving facility of USD 600 million runs to October 21, 2029 and was undrawn at September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 129–130, 135, 137; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C03; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two smaller transactions add assets or vendor support. JetBlue bought 22 LaGuardia slots from Spirit's bankruptcy estate for USD 58.5 million, completed in October 2026 after a USD 6 million deposit, and it received vendor credits of up to USD 105 million from the engine maker, usable until the end of 2027, which lower future cost rather than provide cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by rising secured encumbrance and eroding equity, because new lenders rank ahead of the USD 995 million of unsecured claims while equity falls, which implies lower recovery for unsecured holders and a greater reliance on collateral and liquidity. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any sponsor, dividend or extraction, audited reporting and management's claim of about USD 7 billion of unencumbered assets. Further analysis requires the proxy statement and the executed financing documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8, 11, 47; calculation C01; calculation C05; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for JETBLUE AIRWAYS CORP (JetBlue Airways Corporation, NASDAQ: JBLU) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated fundamental credit profile to Q3 2026, built on the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance analyses and the seven supplied filings and releases. It states no security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The document dates are the signature dates the documents state; filing dates are not stated. No external source was used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: JetBlue's fundamental credit profile is weak: the airline has real franchise assets but its earnings do not cover interest, so creditors depend on USD 1,626 million of cash and investments, a USD 600 million undrawn line and aircraft collateral until margins recover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Derived EBITDA of USD 115 million for the twelve months to September 2026 covers cash interest of USD 493 million only 0.23x, and free cash flow was USD 1,193 million negative. Net debt of USD 7,135 million is as reported at September 30, 2026; pro forma figures for the October 2026 slot purchase and the expected USD 250 million aircraft financing are not established. The primary downside is fuel and labour cost outrunning fares before USD 1,835 million of debt falls due in 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7, 11, 14; calculation F01; calculation F05; calculation F10; calculation F21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings do not support the debt, and that is the central weakness. Derived EBITDA fell to USD 115 million for the twelve months to September 2026 from USD 320 million in FY2025 and covers cash interest paid of USD 493 million only 0.23x; cover of 1.0x would need the twelve-month operating margin to improve from a 6.1% loss to a 2.3% loss, a gain of 3.8 percentage points, and the nine-month margin so far is a 6.6% loss.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; calculation F01; calculation F03; calculation F18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is negative before debt service and the balance sheet has paid for it. Free cash flow for the twelve months to September 2026 was USD 1,193 million negative, and cash and investment securities fell by USD 851 million in nine months to USD 1,626 million, which at the twelve-month burn rate is about 16.4 months of runway, or 22.4 months with the USD 600 million undrawn line. The pro forma effect of the October 2026 slot purchase and the expected USD 250 million financing on cash is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7, 14; calculation F05; calculation F12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity covers the nearest maturities but little more. Cash and investments of USD 1,626 million cover the USD 1,211 million of debt due through 2028 1.34x, but an illustrative run-rate test that repeats the twelve-month cash burn and adds scheduled maturities to the end of 2027 needs USD 2,120 million against USD 2,226 million of cash, investments and the undrawn line, a surplus of only USD 106 million, or 1.05x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 11, 14; calculation F06; calculation F10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk concentrates in 2029, where USD 1,835 million, or 21.9% of scheduled maturities, falls due alongside the October 2029 expiry of the undrawn revolving line. The convertible notes of USD 460 million fall due in September 2029 and the TrueBlue term loan amortises to August 2029, so at most 65.5% of that wall is those two instruments; new money in 2026 has been secured aircraft debt, and with 88.2% of gross debt already secured the funding that matters is secured, not unsecured.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 13–14; 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 130, 135, 137; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F10; calculation F11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Pricing power is real but has not yet covered fuel. Unit revenue rose 18.4% in the third quarter and management says about 87% of the higher fuel cost was recaptured, yet nine-month fuel cost rose USD 798 million against a USD 931 million revenue gain, so operating expense rose USD 1.26 for each USD 1.00 of extra revenue. The operating margin has improved from a 10.0% loss in the first quarter to a 5.1% loss in the third, which is the direction creditors need but not yet the level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–40; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation F08; calculation F18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fuel and labour leave no margin protection. Nothing is hedged, so a 10% fuel price rise would add about USD 376 million over twelve months, which is 3.27x derived EBITDA; fuel was 28.5% and salaries 32.9% of nine-month operating expense, and the pilot and inflight contracts are open or amendable with no cost estimate disclosed. Management guides the fourth-quarter fuel price at USD 4.64 per gallon, 54.7% above the USD 3.00 behind its 2028 earnings target.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 38–41, 53; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-07-28_ex991-earningsreleaseq22026.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation F07; calculation F14; calculation F15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending is the main lever and it is only partly flexible. Capital spending and pre-delivery deposits were USD 969 million for the twelve months to September 2026, 1.34x depreciation; management guides annual spending below USD 1 billion and about USD 850 million for 2026, and firm aircraft commitments of USD 5,372 million include USD 570 million due by the end of 2027. Past delivery deferrals and the sale of the Embraer fleet show management will cut and monetise, but the order book is contractual.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 33, 43; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation F09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The franchise and the asset base, not earnings, carry the recovery case. JetBlue holds seat shares of 26% in Boston, 29% in San Juan and 20% in Fort Lauderdale, loyalty supplies 12.8% of nine-month revenue and USD 8.0bn of aircraft and other assets are pledged, while management claims about USD 7 billion is unencumbered, a figure that cannot be verified. Concentration cuts the other way: 95% of routes touch six focus cities and Northeast disruption lifted costs in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 29–31; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is creditor-neutral rather than creditor-friendly. There is no sponsor, dividend or buyback, which removes leakage, but the financing has been secured, the pledged or committed share of owned property and intangibles rose to 66% from 61%, and equity fell 36.9% in nine months to 8.4% of assets, so the USD 995 million of unsecured debt holds the weakest claim on a shrinking cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8, 11, 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation F11; calculation F16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The recovery case is plausible but unproven. Management expects the fourth-quarter operating margin to improve by 1 to 2 percentage points, sustained operating profit in 2027 and earnings of at least USD 1.00 per share in 2028, but all three are unaudited outlook and the 2028 figure assumes jet fuel well below the current guide.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3; EX-99.1_2026-07-28_ex991-earningsreleaseq22026.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation F14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak reading is that revenue momentum and liquidity are better than the margin suggests. Third-quarter unit revenue rose 18.4% while capacity rose 2.3%, management says about 87% of the higher fuel cost was recaptured, and the adjusted operating margin improved to a 3.9% loss from a 4.1% loss a year earlier. JetForward is said to have added USD 470 million of cumulative earnings to June 2026 toward USD 850 million to USD 950 million a year by the end of 2027. Liquidity of USD 2.2bn includes an undrawn line to October 2029, a further USD 250 million of aircraft financing is expected, and management says about USD 7 billion of assets are unencumbered, so secured refinancing of the 2029 maturities is plausible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: These points are management statements or unaudited, and the unencumbered figure is not reconciled with the 66% of owned property and intangibles that the quarterly report says is pledged or committed. The view would improve if the fourth-quarter margin gain of 1 to 2 percentage points arrives with fuel near the USD 4.64 guide, the USD 250 million financing funds, cash and investments stop falling and the 2027 operating profit stays on track. It would worsen if cash and investments approach the USD 1,211 million of maturities due through 2028, if remaining unencumbered assets are given a first lien, or if pilot and inflight settlements add cost without matching fare recapture.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The company states no EBITDA, so every cover and leverage conclusion rests on a small derived figure that moves sharply with any reclassification; interest cover is the steadier test and leverage multiples are quoted only as supporting evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No forward model, peer set or market price was supplied, so the downside is qualitative with one run-rate test, and it cannot size the cushion at other fuel prices or show how the market would price a 2029 refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant test levels are not printed, so the runway conclusions assume the undrawn line and the cash balance are fully usable; a minimum-liquidity or minimum-balance test could bind before cash is exhausted and shorten the runway.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The conclusion that secured funding remains available relies on management's statement of unencumbered assets, which the filings do not itemise, and on one completed aircraft financing, so the refinancing view is judgement rather than demonstrated market access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The cost of the pending pilot and inflight settlements and the earnings contribution of the JetForward programme are not disclosed in audited form, so the margin recovery path is not tested for either.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five strongest supports, in order, are pricing and unit-revenue momentum, with third-quarter unit revenue up 18.4% and loyalty revenue up 13.1% in nine months; liquidity of USD 2.2bn with an undrawn line to October 2029; an owned fleet of 298 operating aircraft, 288 of them owned, with USD 8.0bn of assets pledged and management citing about USD 7 billion unencumbered; a network and loyalty franchise concentrated in six focus cities with seat shares of 26% in Boston and 20% in Fort Lauderdale; and the absence of any sponsor, dividend or buyback together with annual capital spending guided below USD 1 billion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 33–34, 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The five heaviest constraints, in order, are earnings that cover cash interest only 0.23x; negative free cash flow of USD 1,193 million funded by a USD 851 million fall in cash and investments in nine months; unhedged fuel, where a 10% rise costs about USD 376 million, and open labour contracts, with salaries and benefits at 35.1% of nine-month revenue; a structure that is 88.2% secured with the pledged share rising to 66% from 61%; and thin equity, at 8.4% of assets after a 36.9% fall, with USD 1,835 million of debt due in 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–8, 11, 47, 53; calculation F01; calculation F07; calculation F11; calculation F15; calculation F16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: JetBlue is a point-to-point passenger airline with 298 operating aircraft, six focus cities and a loyalty programme, selling mainly leisure and visiting-friends-and-relatives travel in the Northeast, Florida and the Caribbean. Passenger travel is 84.9% of nine-month revenue and loyalty-related revenue 12.8%, which gives some visibility through prepaid tickets and card spending, but demand is discretionary, seasonal and exposed to weather and air traffic control in the home market. The model supports debt service only when unit revenue covers fuel and labour, and at present it does not, so cash-flow visibility rests on advance bookings and the loyalty programme rather than on operating profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 47; calculation F17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: JetBlue is a widely held public company with no sponsor, controlling holder or dividend in the supplied filings, so there is no leakage to owners and no owner to support creditors. JetBlue Airways Corporation is the issuer or borrower of the instruments the notes describe, with JetBlue Loyalty LP as co-issuer of the loyalty financing and unnamed subsidiary guarantors; who owns that partnership and which subsidiaries guarantee are not stated. Business & governance assessed sponsor and governance risk as Medium because ownership and board facts are missing, not because of observed extraction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is discretionary, cyclical and concentrated in a congested home region, but it is not structurally declining. FY2025 revenue fell 2.3% on weaker demand and tariff uncertainty, then nine-month 2026 revenue rose 13.7%, mostly on price: third-quarter yield rose 21.2% and average fare 19.2% while revenue passengers rose 2.2% and load factor fell 1.5 percentage points. Domestic and Canadian flying is 60.4% of nine-month revenue and Caribbean and Latin America 34.0%, so regional shocks in the Northeast, Florida or the Caribbean reach most of the revenue. Price recovery protects margin only if fares keep pace with fuel, which they did for about 87% of the increase in the third quarter by management's measure. Tickets and credits expire within about a year and the air traffic liability of USD 2,696 million is 1.66x cash and investments, so bookings fund operations until they weaken.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 81, 86–87, 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 27, 34; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are not resilient to input shocks because the largest costs are either unhedged or contractually rising. Fuel was 28.5% of nine-month operating expense and salaries, wages and benefits 32.9%, and fuel was unhedged at September 30, 2026. Unit cost excluding fuel rose 7.0% in the third quarter against capacity growth of 2.3%, with about four points of disruption cost from weather and air traffic control, and the pilot contract has been amendable since February 2025. Operating expense rose USD 1.26 for each USD 1.00 of extra revenue in nine months, so operating leverage is currently negative. Costs can be defended only through fares and capacity discipline, and management cut planned second-half capacity by at least two to three points for that purpose.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20, 36–41, 53; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-04-28_ex991-earningsreleaseq12026.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation F08; calculation F15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Derived EBITDA does not convert into free cash flow because cash interest, capital spending and pre-delivery deposits exceed it several times. Nine-month operating cash flow was USD 273 million negative even though a USD 323 million rise in air traffic liability helped it, capital spending and deposits were USD 624 million, and net cash interest was USD 372 million; the twelve-month free cash flow of USD 1,193 million negative compares with FY2025 at USD 1,216 million negative. Capital spending of USD 969 million over twelve months is 1.34x depreciation, and operating lease obligations of USD 1,499 million sit outside debt. Flexibility exists because management has deferred deliveries before and guides spending below USD 1 billion a year, but USD 5,372 million of firm commitments for 77 aircraft run to 2030 and beyond.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7, 17, 33, 43, 46; calculation F05; calculation F09; calculation F13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Rivalry is intense and rivals are larger: the annual report says most competitors have greater financial resources, and industry consolidation or capacity added in JetBlue's focus cities can undo yield gains, which matters because pricing is carrying the margin recovery. Spirit's exit from Fort Lauderdale is described by management as one of the most significant opportunities in years, which helps unit revenue until others redeploy capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - New entry is limited by airport access rather than capital: slots at JFK and LaGuardia, 30 Boston gates and a Terminal 5 lease to 2042 protect the network, and the 22 LaGuardia slots bought for USD 58.5 million add to it, but the bankruptcy of Spirit, the seller, shows that access alone does not make fares profitable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Substitutes are a limited threat: the annual report cites surface transport and video conferencing, which matter most when the economy is weak, and they are less relevant on the Caribbean, Latin American, transcontinental and transatlantic routes that make up 67.6% of 2025 capacity, so substitution is not a primary credit driver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Buyer power is high: leisure customers compare fares, and the loyalty programme and co-brand cards are the main tools that blunt it, which is why loyalty revenue growth of 13.1% in nine months matters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Supplier power is high: four aircraft and engine types from Airbus, Pratt & Whitney and IAE support every flight, two aircraft were grounded for engine availability at September 30, 2026 and the Fly-Fi service depends on one antenna supplier, so a fleet defect cannot be diversified away.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy and macro factors are a primary credit driver here, because they set fuel, capacity and cost. Political and regulatory: air traffic control shortages and slot rules constrain Northeast capacity, federal rules require US citizen control, tariffs on aircraft and parts could raise fleet costs, and the company cites Middle East conflict as a source of fuel volatility. Economic: fuel is the dominant sensitivity and the interest-rate exposure is smaller, with USD 2.1bn of floating-rate debt so that a 100 basis point rise would add about USD 21 million of annual interest. Social: 49% of crewmembers are unionised and new groups have organised in 2026, which raises the cost of settlements. Technological: a new revenue management system and a premium cabin programme are supporting yield, but their contribution is management's claim.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: Boston, San Juan and Fort Lauderdale seat shares and airport access; loyalty revenue up 13.1% and a premium product; an all-Airbus fleet with 288 of 298 aircraft owned; liquidity of USD 2.2bn with an undrawn line to October 2029; and no sponsor leakage. Weaknesses: cover of 0.23x, negative free cash flow, unhedged fuel, labour exposure, a structure that is 88.2% secured and equity at 8.4% of assets. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: Fort Lauderdale growth after Spirit's exit, the United partnership and BlueFirst premium cabin, and fuel falling toward the USD 3.00 assumption. Threats that could weaken it: fuel at the USD 4.64 fourth-quarter guide or higher, union settlements, Northeast disruption, engine groundings and delivery delays, and the Northeast Alliance antitrust case, whose loss cannot be estimated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_jblu-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21, 29–33, 47; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation F11; calculation F16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is weak on coverage, free cash flow, leverage and equity, and adequate only on near-term liquidity. The main supports are USD 2.2bn of liquidity, no maturity larger than USD 582 million before 2029 and USD 8.0bn of pledged assets plus management's claim of about USD 7 billion unencumbered against USD 8,450 million of debt; the constraints are cover of 0.23x, negative cash flow, a secured-heavy structure and a shrinking cushion. The trend within 2026 is mixed: the operating margin improved from a 10.0% loss in the first quarter to a 5.1% loss in the third, but net debt rose to USD 7,135 million from USD 6,552 million at year-end 2025, as reported and before the pro forma effects of the October 2026 slot purchase and the expected fourth-quarter financing, which are not established. The key missing datapoints are covenant levels, a company-defined EBITDA, the cost of open labour contracts and any rating or market price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6, 11, 14, 47; calculation F01; calculation F11; calculation F18; calculation F21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the outlook turns on fuel against fares. Management guides the fourth quarter to 18.0% to 22.0% unit revenue growth and a 1 to 2 percentage point margin gain, full-year adjusted operating margin of a 4.5% to 6.5% loss and sustained operating profit in 2027; tailwinds are Spirit's exit, loyalty and card growth and BlueFirst from December 8, 2026, and headwinds are fuel guided at USD 4.64 per gallon for the fourth quarter, labour talks, Northeast disruption and a USD 1,211 million maturity run through 2028. Over three to five years the 77 firm aircraft deliveries, the 2029 maturity cluster and the 2028 earnings target are the defining items: delivery of the order book adds capital needs just as USD 1,835 million of debt falls due, while the earnings target assumes fuel at USD 3.00 per gallon. Each tailwind supports revenue and margin; each headwind pressures cash flow and refinancing confidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3; EX-99.1_2026-07-28_ex991-earningsreleaseq22026.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 17, 32–33; calculation F10; calculation F14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with fuel staying near the USD 4.64 fourth-quarter guide through the winter while Northeast weather and engine groundings cut completed capacity again and the pilot and inflight settlements add cost. Fare recapture then falls short of the 87% reached in the third quarter, so the operating margin stalls near the 5.1% loss of the third quarter instead of improving by 1 to 2 percentage points, and free cash flow keeps running near the USD 1,193 million negative twelve-month rate. Cash and investments of USD 1,626 million fall toward the USD 1,211 million of maturities due through 2028; covenants on minimum liquidity and minimum balances, whose levels are not printed, could bind before cash is exhausted. Management levers are capital spending cuts, further secured financing including the USD 250 million expected in the fourth quarter, delivery deferrals and capacity cuts, and resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis through 2027 only if those levers are used. The primary downside path is cash burn from unhedged fuel and labour cost into the 2029 maturity cluster, financed by ever more secured debt that pushes the USD 995 million of unsecured debt further back in the queue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_jblu-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 14, 29–33, 47; EX-99.1_2026-10-26_ex991-earningsreleaseq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 3; calculation F05; calculation F06; calculation F10; calculation F11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, JetBlue presents a weak but not hopeless business profile supported by an established Northeast and Caribbean network, a loyalty programme that earns 12.8% of revenue and an unsponsored, undistributing capital policy, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that cover cash interest only 0.23x, negative free cash flow and a structure that is 88.2% secured. Cash-flow durability appears weak because fuel and labour absorb the revenue gains. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on secured aircraft and loyalty-backed funding, on the undrawn line to October 2029 and on delivering the margin recovery management guides. The primary downside path is cash burn into the 2029 maturities of USD 1,835 million. Further analysis would require covenant levels, a lender-defined EBITDA, the proxy statement, ratings and market prices. Fundamental credit is complete. Top risk: unhedged fuel and labour cost outrunning fares while cash and investments fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F01; calculation F10; calculation F11; calculation F17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: All amounts are USD millions unless a row says otherwise; each row shows its inputs and working, and ratios are rounded to two decimals and percentages to one.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two gaps restrict conclusions. Covenant levels, step-downs and headroom are not printed in any supplied source, so the runway conclusions cannot be tested against the loyalty-financing coverage and minimum-liquidity tests or the revolver balance tests, and the company states no EBITDA, so every ratio uses a derived figure. Both are carried as limits on the liquidity and coverage conclusions rather than filled with estimates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No document dated after October 26, 2026 was supplied, so events between that date and the November 5, 2026 cutoff are not established.
